query: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has evolved into one of the most effective structure determination tools in modern day structural biology, achieving in recent years resolutions rivalling those of X-ray crystallography or NMR spectroscopy (Cheng, 2015).

query: Two structure determination methods, based on the molecular dynamics flexible fitting (MDFF) paradigm, are presented that resolve sub-5 Å cryo-electron microscopy (EM) maps with either single structures or ensembles of such structures.
